name: Real-Time Video Chat
tagline: A browser video-chat implementation using WebRTC peer connections, Socket.IO signaling, and a data channel for in-call chat.
description:
This is a two-peer video chat built in the browser. The React client captures camera and microphone with getUserMedia, creates an RTCPeerConnection, and exchanges SDP offers/answers plus ICE candidates through a Socket.IO signaling server.

The Express server does not mix media. It only keeps rooms and forwards signaling messages. Google public STUN servers are used for ICE. A WebRTC data channel carries text chat once the peer connection is up. Signaling is wired to localhost, so this is a working implementation rather than a hosted production service.

coverImage.alt: Real-time video chat WebRTC application — no product screenshot uploaded yet

problem: Browsers cannot send live audio and video to each other without a way to negotiate a peer connection. That means signaling for SDP and ICE, camera/microphone access, and a path for ICE candidates — none of which a normal HTTP API provides on its own.
approach: Use WebRTC for media and a thin Socket.IO server for signaling. Rooms are in-memory sets of socket IDs. Offers, answers, and ICE candidates are forwarded to everyone else in the room. The client queues ICE candidates until a remote description exists, and uses Google STUN servers for candidate gathering. There is no TURN server in this implementation.
solution: A Vite + React frontend and an Express + Socket.IO backend. Users join a room ID, start a call (createOffer + data channel), and see local/remote video plus connection state. Text messages go over an RTCDataChannel named chat. Cleanup closes the peer connection, stops tracks, and disconnects the socket.
outcome: The signaling and peer-connection flow is implemented end to end for a local two-person call. It is not deployed, CORS is limited to localhost:5173, and there is no TURN fallback — so it should be read as a WebRTC implementation, not a production calling product.
features: Camera and microphone capture via getUserMedia
ICE candidate exchange, including queuing until remote description is set
Google STUN servers for ICE gathering
Socket.IO rooms for signaling (join, offer, answer, ice-candidate, user-left)
Remote stream attached to a video element on ontrack
WebRTC data channel for peer-to-peer text chat
Connection status and error reporting in the UI
architecture: React client ⇄ Socket.IO (localhost:5000) ⇄ Express signaling server. Media path is peer-to-peer: getUserMedia → RTCPeerConnection.addTrack → remote ontrack. Signaling events: join-room, offer, answer, ice-candidate. ICE uses stun.l.google.com / stun1.l.google.com. Chat uses an RTCDataChannel, not the signaling server.
